newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson comfortable with estimates.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson comfortable with estimates.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Tuesday it is comfortable with analysts' revised estimates for its earnings from operations to rise to about $3.00 a share this year, excluding a charge taken in the first quarter.
"Three dollars from operations is a reasonable expectation from today's vantage point," Dayton Hudson chief financial officer Douglas Scovanner said in an interview.

Dayton Hudson, parent of Target discount stores, earlier reported its earnings rose to $105 million, or $0.44 a share, during the first quarter ended May 3 from $41 million, or $0.16 a share, a year earlier.
The first-quarter results included an after-tax charge of $21 million, or $0.09 a share, for debt redemption costs. Without the charge, the company earned $126 million, or $0.53 a share.

Wall Street analysts had expected Dayton Hudson to earn about $0.40 a share without the charge, Scovanner said. And many analysts raised their estimates for Dayton Hudson's full-year earnings after the quarterly results were released.
Including the charge for debt redemption, the company's net income for the full year is expected to rise to about $2.90 a share, and the company is comfortable with that estimate, he said.
In 1996 Dayton earned $463 million or $1.95 per share, including an after-tax charge of $81 million for real estate repositioning costs and an $11 million after-tax charge for debt redemption.
